Dear Hamda*,* 



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *26 December 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Account and Profile*
* *Billing Details* 
* *Blocks*
* *Communications*
* *Consents* 
* *Identity Verifications*
* *Order History Security* 



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Dear Marija,

Thank you for you data subject rights requests.

In relation to your request to delete your Bolt account, to reiterate - irregular activities were detected on your account which prevent us from deleting it. Applicable law permits us to deny your erasure request because the processing is necessary for fraud prevention and to exercise or defend legal claims. As such, the data contained on your account will be retained in accordance with Bolt’s retention policies and practices. You will also be unable to create a new Bolt account using the contact details you previously provided.

In relation to your request for further information on the irregular activities that were detected on your account, we detected signals of fraudulent behaviour on your Bolt account. We are unable to share any further information in this regard, as to share confidential information on the specific indicators that lead to account suspensions or blocks could allow third parties to circumvent such indicators, which in turn would undermine the security of the Bolt platform and threaten the rights and freedoms of other Bolt users.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

+As a general guidance+:

*1. Form of company*: two independent drivers can be part of the same company only if it is registered as a “SAS” or “SARL”. On the contrary, a “microentreprise” is an individual enterprise, therefore only one person can be registered as a director. 

*2. Structure: SAS vs Fleet:* 

* Where the company is a SAS with two independent drivers, as long as each driver owns and exploits their vehicle, then this is not a fleet. The drivers work independently in the name of the SAS.
* Where the company is a SAS that is structured as a fleet, the vehicles are owned by the SAS or are rented by the SAS. The company will centralise the management of the vehicles and the drivers will be considered as employees or service providers. 

If you come across this situation again, going forward you will need to (1) verify the form of the company, and (2) make sure that each driver is the owner of their vehicle. 



+For this situation+:

🇪🇪  *Estonia*

In December, 19 BPO reviews were submitted, and 7 were validated by market specialists. I analysed the differences in the buckets, focusing on the lowest-rated elements and understanding why, in some cases, the BPO rated elements lower than the validators.

*Customer-critical bucket*

There was a difference of 12.03 between BPO and validators, with validators giving lower ratings. The lowest-rated element by validators was _Tone & Empathy_, with a gap of 18.80 compared to BPO. Similarly, the _Relevant Information & Questions_ element was rated lower by validators, with a difference of 15.79. 

Tone & Empathy: Validators have noticed problems with tone and empathy. Sometimes the tone sounds unnatural or too formal, and other times empathy is missing or doesn’t fit.

Relevant Information & Questions: The main reason validators are deducting points is missing information. For example, not informing the reporting party about the phone call.

*Business-critical bucket*

While the scores were quite close, with a small difference of 0.67, BPO rated some of the elements lower than validators. The highest difference was seen in elements like _Safety Logging_ and _Backend Actions_. Validators rated _Compensation Actions_ the lowest, with a big difference of 66.67 compared to BPO ratings.

Safety Logging: It was good to see that validators spotted issues like the tool not being opened on time and problems with tool information. However, spot checks showed that both validators and BPO gave a thumbs-up to elements that should have been rated down. The checks also showed that BPO repeatedly used the 'other safety logging issues' root cause when validators gave a thumbs-up. Without comments, it’s hard to understand why some elements were rated down.

Backend Actions: In some cases, both BPO and the validator noticed the same backend action issues, like a missing admin order comment. However, BPO rated the element down more often than the validator, using the 'wrong backend actions' root cause. Since many actions can fall under this element, it was hard to understand what BPO specifically meant without comments.

*Compliance-critical bucket*

This bucket had the largest difference between BPO and validators, with a gap of 19.10.  Double-validation spot checks confirmed that BPO gave lower ratings, but sometimes these seemed too strict or not accurate. The BPO also gave lower ratings than validators for _Internal Information Handling_, _User Verification_, and _Attachment Handling_.

For internal information handling, it wasn’t clear why BPO scored the element down. During the double checks I didn’t find any errors with the information shared. However, for user verification, BPO rated the element down because the correct process wasn’t followed. In many cases, agents greeted the user by their first name instead of asking for their full name for verification.

*How to provide user LICP flag to Fraud rules input?*

1️⃣ *Call feature flag*

Steps:

* Extend {{RentalAdditionalData}} interface
* Add classic AdditionalDataLoader in parallel
** it accepts {{user_id}} from Request as input
** it should call targeting to check if a user has LICP membership
* Add mock for additional targeting call (not fun considering that there are many targeting calls and we should ensure mocks are created in correct order)

PROS:

* doesn’t require changes on MM side and redeploy

CONS:

* We depend on specific implementation. Current implementation is to use feature flag based on authentication groups to maintain list of LICP users
** If it will be decided to change this implementation, it would be needed to change in several places: MM, Commerce/Payments, Commerce/Fraud
* We would like to move all data collecting to FDGW, so this design looks temporal or we need to implement it on FDGW side from the beginning
* Additional {{targeting}} call may add additional duration. However, in average {{targeting}} responses in 2-3 ms. So, timeout issues we observe sometimes may be related to event loop lag (and not to targeting problems)

2️⃣ *Provide user LICP flag via Request*

Steps:

* Call feature flag somewhere on MM side
* Include {{is_LICP_user}} flag into {{input: MakePreAuthInput}} [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4c1e6fa5a965866842eafbc8de49a0e7e619f496/src/rental/marketplace/rental_order_client/main/client/service/CommerceGatewayService.ts#L46]
* Use {{RentalOrderRequest.order_items}} to provide the flag
* Extend {{RentalOrderInput}} to include new {{is_LICP_user}} user flag
* Modify {{order_items}} parsing on Fraud side
* (maybe) modify existing tests to include new Request parameter
* add new test to ensure that new Request parameter is parsed correctly from {{order_items}}

PROS:

* Doesn’t depend on specific implementation. If the source of LICP users change in future, the change should be done only on MM side (no changes on Fraud side)
* Doesn’t require FDGW migration/implementation

CONS:

* Providing additional Request parameters via {{order_items}} is confusing and not typesafe
** We should use this approach until we remove {{user_rental_order}} checkpoint call from CGW
* Requires small change on MM side and re-deploy

Notes:

* In future we may want:
** remove {{user_rental_order}} checkpoint integration with CGW
** Extract all {{order_items}} parameters to Request interface



*Decision*

We proceed with option 2️⃣ as it looks more correct long-term

Changes done:

# reduced the cable housing holder part diameter to get rid of the play
# added an angled cut to the brake cable channel so that there would be no interference between the cable and the lever body
# Added a cut to the lever body to make replacing the brake cable easier
# added material to the mating surface of the lever blade and the lever body to make the lever blade sit closer to the handlebar so that users with smaller hands could reach the brakes easier.

Currently the idea is to replace the alignment feature with two simple round pins which would work on both Dragon and e-bike handlebar. The height of the pins can be very low (1~1.5mm) so that we do not have to cut through the e-bike handlebar to add these features.
# Solve one issue with the new design: when the lever blade is moved closed to the handlebar, the position of the brake sensor will also change. There are a couple of ways to deal with this problem, but we have to involve the supplier to check which is the easiest option:

## Modify the sensor (least likely to happen because it is most likely a standard part produced in millions)

current version of offer for Poland - 



We are still in progress of reviewing and collecting fdbk on value prop proposal for launch of Bolt Plus in select cities in Poland (Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw), but sharing a WIP version as FYI for an idea of what it may look like :

* Subscription price: 12.99 PLN (same as Uber One, around 3.1 eur, although subscriptions in PL currently are all food-based) with 1 month free trial (or 2 weeks free if we want to be frugal)
* Value prop:
** 15% cashback + 20% cashback on airport rides, scheduled rides and premium category rides
** 3x free cancellations
** priority pick up
** (not advertised) premium customer support

*Rationale for offer (based on Warsaw numbers)*

* we aim to lock in 20% GMV
* 46% of users take 3+ rides per month in Warsaw.
* with 20% expected segment adoption, we'd get user adoption of about 9.2%, which would mean conservatively 18.4~20% GMV adoption (based on other market data)
* user economics: users taking 3+ rides/mo., would benefit *€*0*.*7 from cashback benefit only (potentially more from free cancellations)

Hello Diana,

All in all, the reason for all those specifics is that Ukraine has a unique set up due to legal reasons. Based on our documentation, Ukraine operates based on intermediary model but in fact it’s neither intermediary nor resale but something quite unique which leads to many  specifics.

# Actual debt is not reflecting on Admin, because on local OPS request Commerce manually reset company balances for all UA postpaid clients no matter if the payment was done or not. The reason for such approach is that based on the contract we have with clients they have up to 3 months to pay their debt instead of 1 month as we have on other markets. I checked with local OPS and they confirmed that it’s technically and logically not possible to make changes to Admin considering this set up. 
# Yep, I mean contract. The thing is that all postpaid UA clients has agreement with 2rd party company that represents Bolt on the market (something related to local laws and from legal perspective the only available approach). If the cstr wants to terminate the contract, it means, it needs to be terminated with 3rd party company with the confirmation from our side. 
# Yes, after the escalation, updated data is not only updated on our side but also directed to 3rd party by AM.
# As mentioned before, for Ukraine it’s different than for other markets as clients have an agreement not with Bolt but with a 3rd party company that represents Bolt on the market and it’s not exactly the same set up as intermediary model on other markets.
# For invoice correction, I think your approach is indeed more logical.
# In all honesty, I’m not 100% sure why actual service fee info is not visible in Admin but I checked with local OPS several times and they told me that it’s somehow related to tax regulations and the way invoices are created for the clients. As far as I understand, if it is added to Admin it can mess up data that is later sent to 3rd party company that prepares invoices.
# Yep, there is a legal reason as well as technical one. As mentioned before, debt payment period for UA clients is 3 months which is stated in their contracts and from technical perspective it is impossible to set it up in Admin thus balance in Admin reseted manually every month by Commerce.
# If cstr wants to be switched from CC to postpaid, they need to sign an agreement with 3rd party company that represents Bolt on the market which requires direct involvement of local OPS.
# Most clients know how to access invoices but it may happen that the invoice is not available on the 3rd party platform (wasn’t uploaded or some technical issue). In this case we need to involve local OPS to ensure that the invoice is available on the 3rd party platform. 

If you happen to have any additional questions, please, let me know 🙂

Hi [~accountid:5d3ff51eb7f3ac0da80c815c] a couple of weeks ago I got information about this and it seems it is something we have ti comply with. Unfortunately I have not had the time to look deeply. We have had similar requests in the past and we have asked for external legal advice on this (Ellex). Here is what I have found:

*Questions:* 

_Drivers (ridesharing) and couriers (Bolt Food) operate as service providers on Bolt Operations OÜ platforms, and Bolt Operations collects payments from customers on behalf of these service providers._

_Payments are generally made weekly, to a bank account designated by the service provider._

_Almost all couriers and drivers who operate as private individuals in Estonia have a business account at LHV Bank - this is a prerequisite for registration._

_We have received instructions from bailiffs in various regions to stop paying the service provider and transfer the amount due to the service provider to the bank account designated by the bailiff._

_To simplify the situation: a bailiff contacts us and asks us to transfer the amount of money owed to the courier to his bank account. (1) does the bailiff have the right to demand that Bolt Operations change the service provider's bank information/payment details? (2) if Bolt Operations changes the service provider's account at the bailiff's order, is such an action in line with PSD2 regulation? (3) if Bolt Operations changes the service provider's payment details, what direct risks might such an action create for Bolt Operations?_

*Answers*

* Yes, the attachment notices as well as the enforcement agent’s instructions in the attachment notices are mandatory for Bolt Operations OÜ (“*Bolt*”). By making a payment to the enforcement agent’s payment account, Bolt is deemed to have performed its obligation before the courrier/driver (§ 111 of the Code of Enforcement Procedure; § 76(1) and (3) of the Law of Obligations Act). For the sake of clarity, this only applies with respect to valid attachment notices issued by enforcement agents. Caution should be exercised with respect to complying with any other similar instructions (e.g. instructions by e-mail or from any other party).
* In case of incompliance with the attachment notice, the enforcement agent may impose a penalty payment to Bolt (up to EUR 767 in the first instance and up to EUR 1917 from the second instance; § 26^1^(1) and (4) of the Code of Enforcement Procedure). Furthermore, where Bolt does not comply with the attachment notice, the creditor (of the courrier/partner) is also entitled to submit a claim against Bolt to the court for payment (§ 118(1) of the Code of Enforcement Procedure) and claim also damages for any loss that results from incompliance with the attachment notice (Bolt does not perform its obligation to the enforcement agent; 117(2) of the Code of Enforcement Procedure).
* Attachment of the courrier/driver’s claim against Bolt should also not affect the ongoing setting off of different fees between Bolt and the courrier/driver (we understand that pursuant to T&Cs Bolt’s agency fees are netted against payments that Bolt makes to courriers/drivers), as the courrier/drivers’ are entitled pursuant to the T&Cs only to the balance. Therefore, only the balance can be subject to an attachment.
* From a PSD2 perspective, we do not see any specific risks in complying with the attachment notice (and enforcement agent’s instructions) where Bolt makes payments to the courriers/drivers within an agency relationship, i.e. Bolt relies on the commercial agent exemption or payments from Bolt to courriers/drivers are not seen as payment transactions executed on behalf of users. Either way the PSD2 does not apply.
* From a practical perspective, we see that complying with the attachment notice (and making payments of the courrier/driver’s balances to the enforcement agent instead) may result in at least some of the affected courriers/drivers terminating the use of Bolt’s platform(s) as this may affect the courriers/drivers’ incentive to continue to use the platform(s) (earn money). Especially where the courrier/driver otherwise would prefer to avoid/escape fulfilling its obligations towards its creditors. However, that should not be the case where courriers/drivers are accepting cash directly from users.

[~accountid:5d3b12432acc2d0c6219ff80] What if the car is used for providing services not only via Bolt but also through other platforms, such as Uber? In this case, is the driver allowed to place ad screens in the car when they are offline from the Bolt platform? How would we enforce compliance - do we rely solely on customer complaints, or implement other types of checks?

I am trying to assess whether the prohibition is proportional.

It seems more reasonable to argue that the driver should not display specific ads while providing services ordered via Bolt, as such ads might impact our brand reputation. However, justifying a general prohibition on ad screens, even when the driver is offline from the Bolt platform, seems disproportionate.

Thus, we can justify prohibiting the display of certain ads while the driver is online on the Bolt platform. In such cases, the ad screens could be switched off or removed (if it is possible). However, a complete ban on installing ad screens - especially considering the car might be used on other platforms where we have no involvement - seems excessive. Such a restriction might indeed negatively impact and unjustifiably limit DAD Solutions in offering their services (e.g., screen installations in vehicles), given the significant number of vehicles operating with Bolt in EE.

Is there a way to :

# allow screen installation (if a driver wants so at his own discretion and at his own arrangement with DAD Solutions without our intervention) but with restrictions on the type of ads displayed while the driver is online; or
# generally allow screen installation provided it is completely switched off or removed while the driver is online on the Bolt platform? 

The open question remains - how can we control or enforce this in practice?

Dear Mustapha,

Thank you for your data subject request, which we received on 8 December 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies. For example, we are unable to provide the following, which has been redacted from the copies provided:

* Personal data of Bolt employees contained in transcripts of conversations you had with our Customer Support Team;
* Personal data of other Bolt passengers contained in transcripts of your conversations with passengers and your order history; and

In the attachments, we therefore share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled.

In relation to your payment information, please note the following:

* Regarding your payment information from your current active account as a fleet driver, payments are not made directly to fleet drivers by Bolt; instead, they are processed through their respective fleets. Under relevant data protection legislation, we are permitted to extend the deadline for response by up to an additional two months, which we have determined to be necessary in this instance as we have experienced technical difficulties in retrieving these documents. We apologise for any inconvenience caused by this extension.  We are committed to providing you with the documents as soon as possible. We anticipate that we will be able to provide them by no later than 7 March 2025. If we are able to provide the documents in advance of this date, we will of course do so.

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

We hope you will continue to work with us to resolve any concerns or questions you have. However, if you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data you also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority. In this instance, your local data protection authority is Commission Nationale de l’Informatique et des Libertés (‘CNIL’) with its registered address at 3 Place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France, and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy. You can contact the CNIL using the following means available at [https://www.cnil.fr/en/contact-us|https://www.cnil.fr/en/contact-us]. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Although I would strongly advise to ask this information upfront from the candidate (as this is the market standard and clear legal basis is there for processing this data), then I understand the purpose here and your wish to take the risk. As gender data is not considered special category of data per se, we can rely on legitimate interest (although it could be challenged by regulators and carries a risk). 

I propose the following options: 

*(a)* As we would only like to know the gender division of the applicants (and it would be a subjective observation of the recruiter), is it somehow possible for the recruiters to “mark” the gender somewhere not related with the candidate’s application? I.e. recruiter has 10 candidates they interview during the week and marks the statistics of gender division (e.g. 5 women/5men). Idea would be to create a flow where the data we collect/observe is completely anonymous and cannot be linked to the candidate in any way.  

*(b)* If option (a) is not feasible, then we would collect this information to Greenhouse. However, can we make sure that the retention period for identifiable data is as short as possible? E.g. we gather weekly/monthly stats from the fields and data is deleted after the purpose is achieved? 

With option (b) we should add transparent information to our Privacy Notice that Bolt collects gender data and analyses this to understand the diversity of candidates. 

Let me know how you prefer to proceed.

[~accountid:712020:c0cc6249-3a02-4388-bba0-7e8370980ebe] to make the restriction more proportional and reduce the negative impact of our full restrictions on screen suppliers, I propose the following:

# *Prohibit screens in branded cars:* This aligns with the clause in our T&Cs allowing us to suspend drivers if any activities endanger our reputation. While it would be more balanced to allow screens but prohibit ads while a driver is online, enforcing compliance in practice is challenging. Therefore, prohibiting screens entirely in branded cars seems to be the only option.
# *Allow screens in non-branded cars, with restrictions:* Screens could be permitted in non-branded cars, but ads should be prohibited while drivers are online. While we cannot fully enforce this, we can react to consumer complaints. Additionally, we should inform drivers that displaying ads on screens while providing services via Bolt will be considered a T&C violation and could result in temporary suspension.

This approach is not perfect but provides a more balanced compromise, considering the interests of screen suppliers.

We have reviewed 200 tickets to assess whether agents are following the guidelines outlined in the [+KB article+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408205581330] (if all steps are followed or if there are areas where agents are struggling).Key Findings:

# *Wrong ATI Selection*:

* In 12 cases, agents selected the wrong ATI.

* *5 cases*: These were duplicate cases where the ATI should not have been added, meaning they are not correctly following the [+kB article+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4413476962578?country=global&language=en].

* *7 cases*: These involved general questions on how to verify, where the most appropriate ATI would have been “I have a question about verification.”

# *KB Article Steps Not Followed*:

* *Step 2 (Check for user’s verification data)*:

* In 1 case, the agent marked verification as failed, although the user was successfully verified.

* *Step 3 (Check the verification data)*:

* In 2 cases, agents failed to check the documents provided by the customer.

* *Step 4 (Determine if the user meets the*[ +*market criteria*+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/62125]*)*:

* In 2 cases, agents wrongly escalated the issue to the verification team, even though the market criteria were available in the [+KB article+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/62125].

* *Step 5 (Check the images)*:

* In 1 case, the agent escalated the ticket unnecessarily, as the images clearly showed the person was different.

* *Step 7 (Check the verification status)*:
* In 14 cases, agents failed to provide accurate information about the verification status.

* *9 cases*: Tickets were escalated to the verification team unnecessarily, as the KB article already included information explaining why the verification failed.

In total, the process was not followed correctly in *20 tickets*, with an additional *12 tickets* where the wrong ATI was selected.

# *Quality of Communication*:

* *Customer-Critical Quality*:

* In *46 tickets*, the quality of communication did not meet expectations.

* *Tone and Empathy*:

* In *15 tickets*, the tone and empathy needed improvement. Some messages came across as passive-aggressive and lacked empathy. It’s essential to show friendliness and understanding, especially in cases where verification has failed.

* *Seamless Interaction*:
* In *32 tickets*, issues were identified:

* Missing closing blocks in communications.

* Structural issues, such as messages not being divided into appropriate sections.

* *Providing Relevant Information*:

* In *13 tickets*, agents failed to provide clear explanations or educational information. This included missing guidance on how to properly verify or why the verification failed.

Based on the review, we can conclude that agents are following the guidelines in the [+KB article+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408205581330]. However, there is room for improvement in the *quality of replies* and *adherence to processes*.
Recommendations:

# *Enhance the KB Article*:
#* Include information on why the system triggers users to verify again and the reasons behind this process (it was not provided).
#* Clarify whether agents should consider previous verification attempts when users are triggered to verify again.
# *Improve Communication Quality*:
#* Prepare templates to help agents explain verification outcomes clearly and professionally. For example, users often struggle to understand why their profile is blocked or why verification cannot proceed.

With these changes, we can ensure a more seamless process and improve user satisfaction.

Hi [~accountid:712020:8bcb68bd-f8da-4da1-8320-2536f6bb0c0c] - this is my understanding based on the [guidance issued by the Irish Revenue|https://www.revenue.ie/en/tax-professionals/tdm/income-tax-capital-gains-tax-corporation-tax/part-33/33-03-05.pdf] (5.3.10 DAC7 Nil Return Type “Assumed Nil Return”). See further comments below: 

* According the [FAQ|https://www.revenue.ie/en/companies-and-charities/documents/aeoi/dac7-reg-faqs.pdf],: “_Q3. What is an assumed nil return? A3. An assumed nil return is when a filer declares that there will be another platform operator filing on their behalf. This is done by going to ROS and following the instructions as outlined above. This will bring users to the DAC7 Online Reporting Facility. There, they should select Online Form -> Nil Return -> Assumed Nil Return -> Enter Reporting Period -> Next. From here they can enter the details required, including Name and TIN of assuming platform. Note: DAC7 Foreign Platform Operators should not file an assumed nil return, as the option to assume the filing responsibility for another PO is only available to platforms based in the European Union. FPOs should file on their own behalf._ 
* _FAQ Q4. What is an assuming PO? A4. An assuming platform operator is one that is assuming the responsibility to file on behalf of another platform operator (referred to as the assumed). When filing, the assuming platform operator must provide the details of the assumed platform operator under “Other Platform Operator”._
* Based on the [Revenue guidance|https://www.revenue.ie/en/tax-professionals/tdm/income-tax-capital-gains-tax-corporation-tax/part-38/38-03-31.pdf], Bolt Operations OU should be the assuming platform operator and Bolt ITX is the assumed platform operator: “7.4 Reporting on behalf of another reporting platform operator A reporting platform operator can report the information outlined above on behalf of another reporting platform operator. In this scenario the reporting platform operator which has not reported the information must – a. keep proof, in the form of documentary evidence, that the required information has been reported, and b. declare to Revenue, through the Revenue Online System, by the annual reporting date that another reporting platform operator is reporting the required information on their behalf. This is in line with the DAC7 wording: “Where there is more than one Reporting Platform Operator, any of those Reporting Platform Operators shall be exempt from reporting the information if it has proof, in accordance with national law, that the same information has been reported by another Reporting Platform Operator in another Member State.”

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *17 July 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Thanks for escalating this [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] / [~accountid:621d26539c3cce00694a1b14] . In short, from a Privacy POV:

* *Driver Selfie Verification*: I am discussing with the team and will get back to you ASAP.
** ([~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - when you are back, to avoid duplication of efforts, would you mind pointing me towards previous tickets where we have analysed DSV so that I can ensure consistency?)
* *Audio Trip Recording*: Please confirm how much demand there is an ATR for Belgium (i.e., is is a necessity or a ‘nice to have’?). If there is a need for it, we will need to plan our budget / resources for conducting a privacy / legal assessment, to determine feasibility.
* *Dash cams*: We should not be providing dashcams to drivers. I would also advise against offering discounts to drivers when purchasing dashcams.

See further details below. [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] let me know if there is anything you might add when you are back 🙂 

*Audio Trip Recording*

For some context, before launching ATR in any country, we need to perform a local law analysis. The reason for this analysis is that audio recording is a sensitive feature, and in a number of countries it is forbidden to record audio without consent, or without informing the persons recorded. In some countries, breaching the obligations re audio recording are a criminal offence. 
We have not previously performed an analysis for Belgium, and we haven't been informed about the need/initiative to launch ATR in Belgium. If there is a need for a full analysis of ATR feasibility for Belgium, please let me know, as we would need to plan our budget / resources for this (i.e., it will take a few weeks and we would need to engage local counsel).

*Dash cams*

From a privacy POV, we have taken the position that drivers are independent controllers of any footage recorded on their dashcams - this position allows us to sidestep a lot of privacy law issues that would otherwise arise, and is one we recently reiterated to the Estonian regulator. In order to be able to maintain this position, *we need to be able to demonstrate that we do not exercise any control over the use of the cameras*.
Providing drivers with dashcams to install in their cars could be interpreted as Bolt trying to exercise a form of control, which we need to try and avoid. Although offering discounts to drivers when purchasing dashcams is a step away from this, it still flirts with the same issues.
As such, unless there is a pressing need for this, I would not advise pursuing it for now from a Privacy POV.

*Spark* 

{noformat}WITH acc_details AS 
(
  SELECT 
    ca.id,
    ca.client_id,
    pc.external_id AS driver_id,
    ca.created,
    ca.account_recipient,
    ca.account_iban,
    ca.account_swift,
    LEAD(ca.created) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) AS next_id_created,
    LEAD(ca.id) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) AS next_id,
    CASE WHEN (LEAD(ca.created) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) IS NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS next_null
    FROM ng_payout_spark.invoicing_payment_client_account ca
    JOIN ng_payout_spark.invoicing_payment_client AS pc ON ca.client_id = pc.id 
    WHERE ca.created_date >= date('2023-01-01') AND pc.created_date >= date('2023-01-01')
)
SELECT 
co.country_code|| ':' ||lower((REPLACE(acc.account_recipient,' ',''))) as key,
sum(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_problematic_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_labeled_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE OR co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_total_irregular,
round(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END)/sum(co.user_price_eur),2) AS ratio_problematic,
round(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE OR co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END)/sum(co.user_price_eur),2) AS ratio_irregular,
approx_count_distinct(co.driver_courier_id) AS cnt_unq_drivers,
count(co.order_id) AS cnt_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN acc_details AS acc ON co.created > acc.created AND co.driver_courier_id = acc.driver_id
    AND CASE WHEN acc.next_null = 0 THEN co.created <= acc.next_id_created ELSE co.created > acc.created END
WHERE
lower(REPLACE(acc.account_recipient, ' ', '')) <> ''
AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATEADD(month, -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS date)
AND co.order_state = 'finished' AND co.order_type ='rides'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING (ratio_problematic > 0.3 OR ratio_irregular > 0.4) and (sum_problematic_eur > 200 or sum_labeled_eur > 400){noformat}

----

Hi Blanche, 

In Belgium, the laws regarding the possibility of advertising on PHVs are strict. As such, branded cars in Belgium only carry the Bolt logo and a legal disclaimer as this represents a sign of affiliation (which is authorized) and not a form of advertisement. 

In June 2023, Bolt BE was the focus of the “Federation Belge des Taxis” (FeBeT) because they were claiming that (1) we were illegally advertising on PHVs; and (2) practicing an act of unfair competition with regards to Taxis. 


To answer your question and in light of this regulatory context, adjusting the current sticker to add a catchy phrase on both sides of the car would be a risk of committing a prohibited activity. You can find hereafter the current design in BE which includes the legal disclaimer to use: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yxBarCT4KHlAZSY-4SrpXY2uUamTRiHU/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yxBarCT4KHlAZSY-4SrpXY2uUamTRiHU/edit|smart-link] 

If the objective is to make it more obvious that we are a ride-hailing company, perhaps we can add a description to the logo and the disclaimer: i.e. “Bolt - Intermédiaire de Réservation”.

Please let me know if you have any further questions on this. 

Thank you

Dear Sylvia,

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *28 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*
* *Identity Verifications*
* *Billing Details*
* *Account and profile*
* *Communications*
* *Consents*
* *Security*
* *Blocks*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Hello [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] I've checked and the driver is blocked because a rider reported he arrived with a different vehicle. According to the process for UK, the safety agents should have done the following:

* Ask the driver to send us a selfie of themselves holding their PCO badge with the vehicle in the shot for further investigation.
* Confirm how many previous reports of its kind we have against the reported user;
** Check the chat history between driver and rider and whether the driver sent the vehicle details via the in-app chat.
** Check if the driver has previous cancelled trips or rating comments stating the same issue. They would count as precedents.
* If the photo is provided, the vehicle, document, and the driver themselves match the information we have on file in Admin, and there are no precedents the event Cannot Be Confirmed.

Outcome:

* Close the case as advised by the tool. *Do not take deviant action*, unless specified by Case Managers.

And proceed with the blocking based on the following:

* *London:* If you submit a Tool where the consequential action is a block or you have reported the event to the police and chosen Yes on Will or Has Bolt Reported This to the Police? in the Assessment Tool, the Tool will escalate the event to Case Managers. Case Managers will review the event where the driver should be blocked consequently, place the consequential block, inform the driver of the action taken, fill out a PHV105 report and send it to TfL. For police reports, Case Managers will decide whether to report it to the regulator or not.
** *London Black Cabs:* More information about Blocking Matrix, Police Reporting, and Escalation Procedures can be found [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/347384791].

In this case, the tickets are from Zendesk and I don't have access to check them anymore and it would be best, before making any decisions regarding the unblocking, to involve an incident manager for UK in this ticket.

During this task we used the same function to do the {{scan}} calls and we first set the {{count}} parameter to 1000. During the release we observed a very large number of {{scan}} commands(around 20x more than the {{keys}} calls).

!image-20250109-113955.png|width=652,height=315,alt="image-20250109-113955.png"!

This brought some side effects:

# Increase CPU load on the Redis instance
!image-20250109-114045.png|width=778,height=336,alt="image-20250109-114045.png"!
# Increased latencies for /geAllVisibleProviders endpoint from 25ms to 50msP99
!image-20250109-115653.png|width=628,height=220,alt="image-20250109-115653.png"!
# Increase in max event loop lag
!image-20250109-115727.png|width=932,height=310,alt="image-20250109-115727.png"!


The reason: instead on one {{keys}} call we are doing ~20 {{scan}} calls. Why? Reading scan [documentation|https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/] we learn how scan works and we find out that it first select the keys from the memory(number of elements ~= COUNT param). After this step the {{MATCH}}filtering is done. Because of this and because we have around 16k elements in Redis atm. => we need to do ~16-20 {{scan}} calls instead on 1 {{keys}}.

Next idea was to increase the {{COUNT}} parameter to 20K so the {{scan}} function can to it’s magic and behave the same as the {{keys}} function. We just did a canary release and was enough to stop because we say that the {{scan}} command was more time consuming than the {{keys}} command

!image-20250109-123958.png|width=621,height=300,alt="image-20250109-123958.png"!

, the CPU usage of the Redis instance has increased 

!image-20250109-124045.png|width=705,height=340,alt="image-20250109-124045.png"!

and the endpoints latencies also started to increase 

!image-20250109-124128.png|width=636,height=684,alt="image-20250109-124128.png"!

Rollback!

Looking at this Redis graph with the number of elements 

!image-20250109-124307.png|width=1381,height=303,alt="image-20250109-124307.png"!

we noticed the dbX legend and we realized that Redis can have multiple DBs in the same instance so let’s store the in-flight providers in a separate DB and this way the {{scan}} command should behave the same as the {{keys}} command and should have a way smaller response time.

And we were right, now the {{scan}} command takes around 3us compared to 2ms of {{keys}} and 7ms of full {{scan}} 

!image-20250109-124750.png|width=825,height=324,alt="image-20250109-124750.png"!

and a nice side effect was the decrease of the CPU load of the Redis instance 

!image-20250109-124843.png|width=1029,height=339,alt="image-20250109-124843.png"!

Conclusion: whenever we store multiple types of objects in Redis and we need to search for stuff (keys or values) it’s better to store these objects in separate DBs if possible.

The 16.2 GBP amount is the capture while the 2.2 GBP is authorized amount which will be released to the customer. 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

Lets take your example - if you define the below

Corp COA to RBKBR (Poland) :

Primary GL 2410+ Spend category -A (Condition dimension & Value) = Alternate ledger 830-9
Primary GL 2620+ Spend category -B (Condition dimension& Value) = Alternate ledger 830-9

RBKBR (Poland) to Corp COA (reversal mapping)

Alternate ledger 830-9 + Spend category - A (Resulting dimension & Value) = Primary GL 2410
Alternate ledger 830-9 + Spend category - B (Resulting dimension & Value) = Primary GL 2620

From the above there are no conditions defined on account 830-9 to identify which primary account (2410 or 2620) should be used. Since there are no conditions, the system will never be able to identify which resulting account to use (and therefore, which resulting values (like spend category category to apply).

Resulting values = the worktags that will be applied to the resulting account once the system identifies which resulting account to use based on the conditions.

Given that the current functionality does not allow for the requirement of mapping multiple primary accounts to one alternate account, the recommendation is to change the mapping to include additional alternate ledger accounts.

{quote}Please describe how exactly we will be using CarScan and for what purposes.{quote}

*Overview of CarScan Usage*
CarScan is a digital inspection tool used in Bolt's vehicle onboarding and verification processes, leveraging AI-driven scoring to evaluate vehicle condition through captured images and inspection inputs. It facilitates accurate, efficient, and consistent inspections, replacing manual methods, and generating comprehensive reports to highlight damages, defects, or compliance issues.

*Primary Purposes of CarScan Usage*

* *Vehicle Inspection Capture*:
** To digitally record vehicle condition during onboarding and periodic inspections.
** Generate a comprehensive inspection report in PDF format for record-keeping and compliance (car profile).
* *Driver and Vehicle Validation*:
** *Driver Information*: ID numbers and phone numbers of the inspecting driver are captured. This data is validated against the government NATIS database when the vehicle is driver-owned.
** *Vehicle Information*: License plate, ownership status, and vehicle details are cross-referenced with NATIS to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

*Secondary Purposes and System Limitations*

* Where car owner phone numbers are not provided during inspections, these are acquired via third-party services to meet system requirements (mandatory field).
* In cities requiring a secondary disc (operating license), CarScan-generated reports include relevant “verification” data for legal and operational compliance.
* Data captured in CarScan is used to improve operational efficiency and document compliance, monitor inspection quality of Bolt fleet, and enhance decision-making.



{color:#bf2600}*What is outstanding?*{color}

** If the inspecting driver does not own the vehicle, CarScan prompts them to input the car owner's name, ID, and phone number (if available).

Hi [~accountid:62b2cf3c0c77011bdfdcdbcd] . Let me share some background.

Around a year ago, we began negotiations with this provider regarding the purchase of map data for the entire country. The provider is an official partner of the government and offers comprehensive, up-to-date map data for the country. Our main competitors (Uber, Yango) have also purchased data from them.

As an initial step, we decided to test their data and started with one city. However, due to a backlog in our internal testing queue, the process took longer than anticipated, and even by the agreed deadline, we were unable to complete our tests.

Now, we have decided to move forward with purchasing map data for five cities, as the initial results were promising. The challenge we face is that the provider is concerned that once we receive the data, we might change our mind and continue using it without formal purchase. As a result, they are requesting that we make the payment before they deliver the full set of data.

{noformat}--------------- /////////// RECIPIENT ////////////// --------


WITH paytopay AS
(
SELECT 
x.*,
CASE WHEN LAG(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS prev_is_null,
CASE WHEN LEAD(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS next_is_null,
LAG(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_id,
LAG(x.crt) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_created,
LAG(x."method") OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_method,
LEAD(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_id,
LEAD(x.crt) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_created,
LEAD(x."method") OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_method
FROM (
		WITH instant AS(
		SELECT
		pp.client_id,
		pc.external_id AS driver_id,
		pp.id,
		pp.created AS crt,
		pp."type",
		pp.target_amount,
		pp.target_currency,
		pp."method",
		pp.state,
		pp.created_date
		FROM glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_payout AS pp
		JOIN glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_client AS pc ON pp.client_id = pc.id 
			WHERE pp."method" = 'instant'
			AND pp.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
		),
		regular AS 
		(
		SELECT
		pp.client_id,
		pc.external_id AS driver_id,
		pp.id,
		date_trunc('day',pp.created) AS crt,
		pp."type",
		pp.target_amount,
		pp.target_currency,
		pp."method",
		pp.state,
		pp.created_date
		FROM glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_payout AS pp
		JOIN glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_client AS pc ON pp.client_id = pc.id
			WHERE pp."method" = 'regular'
			AND pp.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
		)
		SELECT * FROM instant
		UNION ALL
		SELECT * FROM regular
	) AS x 
		WHERE x.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
		ORDER BY x.crt DESC
	)
SELECT 
co.country_code|| ':' ||LOWER(REPLACE(acc.account_recipient,' ','')) AS key,
sum(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_problematic_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_labeled_eur,
sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE OR co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END) AS sum_total_irregular,
round(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END)/sum(co.user_price_eur),2) AS ratio_problematic,
round(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE OR co.driver_courier_fraud_label = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur else 0 END)/sum(co.user_price_eur),2) AS ratio_irregular,
approx_distinct(co.driver_courier_id) AS cnt_unq_drivers,
count(co.order_id) AS cnt_orders
	FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
	LEFT JOIN paytopay AS ptp ON co.created < ptp.crt AND co.created_date <= ptp.created_date
							AND co.driver_courier_id = ptp.driver_id
							AND CASE WHEN 	
										ptp.prev_is_null = 0 THEN co.created > ptp.prev_created
										ELSE
										co.created < ptp.crt 
										END
	LEFT JOIN
			(					
			SELECT 
				ca.id AS account_id,
				ca.client_id,
				pc.external_id AS driver_id,
				ca.created,
				ca.account_recipient,
				ca.account_iban,
				LEAD(ca.created) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) AS acc_next_id_created,
				LEAD(ca.id) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) AS acc_next_id,
				CASE WHEN (LEAD(ca.created) OVER(PARTITION BY ca.client_id ORDER BY ca.id) IS NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS acc_next_null
					FROM ng_payout.invoicing_payment_client_account ca
					JOIN glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_client AS pc ON ca.client_id = pc.id 
				WHERE ca.created_date >= date('2023-01-01')
				) AS acc 
			 		ON CASE WHEN ptp.id IS NOT NULL
			 					THEN ptp.crt > acc.created AND ptp.client_id = acc.client_id AND (CASE WHEN acc.acc_next_null = 0 THEN ptp.crt < acc.acc_next_id_created ELSE ptp.crt > acc.created END)
			 				WHEN ptp.id IS NULL 
			 					THEN co.created > acc.created AND co.driver_courier_id = acc.driver_id AND (CASE WHEN acc.acc_next_null = 0 THEN co.created <= acc.acc_next_id_created ELSE co.created > acc.created END)
							END
WHERE
co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
AND co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
AND co.order_state = 'finished' AND co.order_type ='rides'

GROUP BY 1

Hi [~accountid:623ace37b75ca80070562c04] [~accountid:712020:d57216df-6dcd-48f4-a077-0d148dafa1d4] re the CP & RTT pro-rata rules, please see below applicable scenarios and calculation methods: 

* *RTT* & *CP N* pro-rata for *starters/leavers,* both *daily* and *hourly based*:
_Monthly acquisition /30 * number of calendar days of employment in the month, then rounded up to 2 decimals_.
* *RTT* pro-rata during *Sick & Unpaid Leaves*, only for *hourly based:* 

_RTT normally acquired in the month / number of working days in the month * number of working days actually worked, rounded up to 2 decimals._



There are no other scenarios when RTT or CP N monthly acquisition would be pro-rated.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *28 November 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt
